title: Lipschitz push-forward and straight-line homotopy operators for normal currents near a region (Simon 2.17–2.29, 3.2(2); parent A2, A4, I.6, I.7 and the core of Step 7)
statement: Assume (S5′), the conclusion of the sibling theorem deformation_im_pushforward_limit after its premise LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity: for all P, Q, k, every integer multiplicity X = τ(M, θ, ξ) ∈ D_k(ℝ^P) (IsRectifiableTriple univ k M θ ξ, θ natural-valued on M, X(ω) = tauAction k M θ ξ ω) and every Λ-Lipschitz g : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q with g⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X compact for compact K, there is S ∈ D_k(ℝ^Q) with IsLipschitzPushforward X g S, S integer multiplicity, and ∫_M θ(x)·nVectorPushforward k (Dg_j(x)) (ξ(x)) (ω(g_j(x))) dH^k(x) → S(ω) for every sequence of C¹ maps g_j with a common Lipschitz bound converging uniformly to g and every test form ω. Then for every D ∈ ℕ there are constants c_k ≥ 0 (k ∈ ℕ, depending only on D, k) such that for every map f : ℝ^D → ℝ^D there are operators P_k : D_k(ℝ^D) → D_k(ℝ^D) and H_k : D_k(ℝ^D) → D_{k+1}(ℝ^D) (all k) with the following properties. (I) For every k, closed E ⊆ ℝ^D, Λ ≥ 0, δ > 0, b ∈ ℝ such that f is Λ-Lipschitz on the open δ-neighbourhood thickening δ E and |f(x) − x| ≤ b for x ∈ E, and every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^D) with M(X) < ∞, M(∂X) < ∞ in case k = j + 1 (formally: every Y ∈ D_{j+1} with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X has M(∂Y) < ∞) and spt X ⊆ E: (1) M(P_kX) ≤ c_kΛ^kM(X); (2) M(H_kX) ≤ c_k·b·(1 + Λ)^k·M(X); (3) spt P_kX ⊆ closure f(spt X); (4) spt H_kX ⊆ cthickening b (spt X); (5) if X is integer multiplicity then so are P_kX and H_kX; (6) (tangential vanishing) if α ∈ SimonMultiIndex k D, z ∈ ℝ^D, ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^D), ε > 0, every x ∈ thickening ε (spt X) with f(x) ∈ thickening ε (tsupport ω) satisfies f(x)_i = z_i for all i ∉ range α, and ω(y)(e_{α(1)},…,e_{α(k)}) = 0 for every y, then P_kX(ω) = 0; (7) (linearity) if X₁ ∈ D_k(ℝ^D) satisfies the same hypotheses (M(X₁) < ∞, the boundary condition, spt X₁ ⊆ E) and X₂(ω) = aX(ω) + a₁X₁(ω) for all ω, then P_kX₂(ω) = aP_kX(ω) + a₁P_kX₁(ω) and H_kX₂(ω) = aH_kX(ω) + a₁H_kX₁(ω) for all ω. (II) For every j, E, Λ, δ, b as above and X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^D) with M(X) < ∞, M(∂X) < ∞, spt X ⊆ E: (8) ∂(P_{j+1}X) = P_j(∂X); (9) X(ω) − P_{j+1}X(ω) = ∂(H_{j+1}X)(ω) + H_j(∂X)(ω) for every ω (homotopy from f at t = 0 to the identity at t = 1).
